draft.title: Sex-linked inheritance
card: Females have two X chromosomes (XX). Males have one X and one Y (XY). A sex-linked gene is one carried on the X chromosome.
Red-green colour blindness is caused by a recessive allele on the X chromosome. The Y chromosome carries no matching allele for this gene.
A male has only one X, so a single recessive allele on it will show. A female needs the recessive allele on both of her X chromosomes to show it.

A female with one recessive allele and one dominant allele does not show the trait, but she can pass the recessive allele to her children. A father passes his X to his daughters and his Y to his sons.
draft.remember: Males have one X, so one recessive X-linked allele is enough to show the trait.

a.q: Why is red-green colour blindness seen more often in males than in females?
opts: Males have one X, so one recessive allele shows
Males need two recessive alleles to show the trait
The allele is dominant in males and recessive in females
The allele is carried on the Y chromosome
a.why: The gene is on the X chromosome and the Y has no matching allele, so a male's single recessive allele is not masked. Females have a second X that can carry a dominant allele, which often hides the trait.
a.clue: Think about how many X chromosomes a male has.

b.q: Aisha has normal colour vision but carries one colour blindness allele on an X chromosome. She has a son with a man who has normal colour vision. What is true of their son?
opts: He has a 50% chance of being colour blind
He will certainly have normal colour vision
He will certainly be colour blind
He has a 50% chance of being a carrier only
b.why: Aisha passes either her normal X or her X with the recessive allele to a son, each with equal chance. His father gives him a Y, which cannot mask the allele, so a son who gets the recessive X is colour blind. A male cannot be a carrier only, because the allele would show.
b.clue: A son gets his X from his mother and his Y from his father.

a.best: Males have one X, so one recessive allele shows

b.best: He has a 50% chance of being colour blind

problems.detail: 'A sex-linked gene is one carried on the X chromosome' is too narrow. Sex-linked genes include Y-linked genes as well. Better: 'An X-linked (sex-linked) gene is one carried on the X chromosome', or 'Most sex-linked genes studied are on the X chromosome'.
